 MACA NO.945 OF 2020  3  2025:KER:83693  JUDGMENT Dated this the 5th day of November, 2025

The petitioner in OP (MV) No.1147/2015 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-II, Mavelikara has preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal for the injuries sustained by him in a motor accident that occurred on 04.04.2015.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-II, Mavelikara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as follows:-
On 04.04.2015, while the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on a Motorcycle bearing Registration No.KL- 30D-1423 ridden by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, the same hit a pedestrian and as a result of which the petitioner was thrown on to the road and sustained serious injuries.
3. The rider and owner of the offending motorcycle were arrayed as 1st and 2nd respondents respectively, MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 whereas the insurer was arrayed as the 3 rd respondent.
The 3rd respondent contested the petition and filed a written statement mainly disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.

Moreover, in the written statement it was further contended that at the time of the accident the petitioner himself was riding motorcycle and it was due to his negligence that the accident occurred and hence he is not entitled to be compensated for the injuries sustained in the accident.
Anyhow, the 3rd respondent admitted the insurance coverage for the motorcycle involved in the accident.

Vishnu G vs Harish Gopinathan on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78341669/
2 4.
During trial, the documents produced from the side of the petitioner were marked as Exts. A1 to A19 (series).

The copy of the Insurance Policy produced from the side of the 3rd respondent was marked as Ext.B1.
5.

After trial, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KL-30D-1423 by the 1st respondent and being the MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 insurer, the 3rd respondent was held liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation was quantified at Rs.43,944/- with 8% interest from the date of petition till realisation and proportionate costs.
Challenging the said compensation awarded, the petitioner has come up with this Appeal.
6. I heard Sri. M.V.Thamban the learned counsel for the appellant and Smt. P. Lissy Jose, the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.

7. The learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is too meager and not sufficient to compensate the injuries, hardships and inconveniences suffered by the petitioner due to the accident.

According to the counsel, the Tribunal erred in assessing the monthly income of the petitioner reasonably and as a result,
awarded only a nominal amount as compensation under the head of loss of earnings.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent insurance company, would MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just, fair, reasonable and adequate and hence warrants no interference.
8. From the rival contentions raised, it is gatherable that the main dispute that revolves around this appeal is with respect to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
A perusal of the impugned award reveals that for the purpose of determining compensation under the head of loss of earnings, the Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.5,000/-.
In the petition it is averred that during the relevant period the petitioner was working as a salesman and was earning a monthly income of Rs.10,000/- per month.

Although such an averment was made in the petition,
no documents whatsoever was produced from the petitioner's side to substantiate the claim of the petitioner regarding his occupation and income.
Nevertheless, the accident occurred in the year 2015.

Therefore, having regard to the year of accident and in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the Tribunal ought to have assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.10,000/- notionally.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. As evident from the impugned award, the Tribunal granted compensation towards loss of earnings only for a period of three months.
While considering whether the compensation awarded for loss of earnings for only three months is justified, it becomes necessary to examine the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner.

As evident from the Medical Records, the petitioner had sustained the following injuries in the accident:-
Head injury, lacerated wound 4 cm x 2 cm behind left ear, active bleeding, contusion 2x1 cm rights little finger, fracture left temporal bone, hyperdenisy along the Vishnu G vs Harish Gopinathan on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78341669/

3 tentorium cerebelli, suggestive of bleed, peneumocephaluc present, depressed comminuted fracture involving squamous and mastoid parts of left temporal bone and fracture lateral wall of left orbit and depressed scalp fracture.
MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 10.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
The injury includes fracture of the temporal bone.
Considering the serious nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the view that he would have been prevented from doing any work or earning income at least for six months.
Hence the petitioner is found entitled to get an amount of Rs.10,000/- x 6 as compensation under the head of loss of earnings.

Already an amount of Rs.15,000/-has been awarded by the Tribunal under the said head, after deducting the said amount the petitioner is found entitled to get an amount of Rs.45,000/-as additional compensation under the head of loss of earnings.
11. The nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner speaks for itself regarding the pain and sufferings endured by him due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Of course the same has to be compensated adequately.

A perusal of the award reveals that only a nominal amount of Rs.10,000/-
has been awarded by the Tribunal as MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 compensation under the said head.

It was on the basis of a finding entered on by the Tribunal that the petitioner was not holding a valid driving license at the time of the accident, the Tribunal limited the compensation under the head of pain and sufferings to Rs.10,000/-.

While considering the sustainability of the said finding, it is to be noted that though in the written statement the respondent Insurance Company, took a contention that the petitioner was actually riding the motorcycle at the time of the accident, this contention stands disproved by the final report filed by the police.
In the final report it is specifically recorded that the motorcycle involved in the accident was ridden by the 1st respondent at the relevant time.
Therefore, the contention of the Insurance Company that the petitioner was riding the motorcycle at the time of the accident cannot be sustained.
However, the Tribunal proceeded on an erroneous assumption that it was the petitioner who was riding the motorcycle.
I am of the considered view that the compensation awarded by the MACA NO.945 OF 2020 2025:KER:83693 Tribunal under the head of pain and suffering is on the lower side.
However, I am cognizant of the fact that only an amount of Rs.15,000/- has been claimed in the petition as compensation under the said head.

Nevertheless, while considering a petition filed under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation, it is incumbent upon the court to ensure that the compensation awarded by it is just fair, reasonable and adequate irrespective of the claim made by the parties.
Therefore, the amount of compensation claimed in a motor accident claim petition is of little consequence while awarding compensation.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment procedures underwent by him I am of the view that he is entitled to get an amount of Rs.50,000/- as compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.
After deducting the already awarded amount of compensation under the head of pain and suffering, the petitioner is found entitled to get an additional compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the said head.

4 12.

sentences.text: Likewise, it is pertinent to note that the Tribunal omitted to award any amount as compensation under the head of loss of amenities and enjoyment of life.

While awarding compensation, the Tribunal ought to have considered the inconveniences and hardships met by the petitioner due to the injuries sustained in the accident and a reasonable amount ought to have been awarded under the said head.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the period of inpatient treatment undergone by him, I am of the view that, in the interest of justice, an amount of Rs.30,000/- has to be awarded as compensation under the head of loss of amenities and enjoyments in life.
13. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other various heads appears to be reasonable and no interference is warranted in respect of those heads.

Hence an amount of Rs.1,15,000/-
(Rs.45,000/- + Rs.40,000/-+ Rs.30,000/-) has to be added towards the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

In the light of the aforesaid observations and findings,
the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of Rs.1,15,000/- (Rupees One Lakh and Fifteen Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The respondent Insurance Company is ordered to deposit the enhanced compensation with interest before the Tribunal with proportionate costs, within a period of three months from the date of this judgment.

Immediately on the compensation amount being deposited, the Tribunal shall, after deducting the liability of the appellant/petitioner towards court fee, disburse the compensation amount to the appellant/petitioner in accordance with law.

Sd/-
